title: Establece requisitos fitosanitarios de importación para frutos frescos para consumo de naranja (citrus sinensis) procedentes de Egipto
description:
• El proyecto de resolución establece los requisitos fitosanitarios para la importación a Chile de frutos frescos para consumo de naranja ( Citrus sinensis ) de origen y procedencia Egipto.
     
  • La medida establece que los envíos deberán estar amparados por un Certificado Fitosanitario Oficial emitido por la Organización Nacional de Protección Fitosanitaria de Egipto, incluyendo declaraciones adicionales para las plagas cuarentenarias asociadas a la vía.
     
  • Para el manejo del riesgo de Bactrocera zonata y Ceratitis capitata se establece la aplicación de un tratamiento cuarentenario de frío T107-L, a una temperatura de 1,67 °C o inferior durante 18 días, el cual podrá realizarse en origen o en tránsito. Asimismo, se establecen medidas fitosanitarias específicas para Phytophthora palmivora y requisitos de inspección para las restantes plagascuarentenarias reguladas.

 

  • Los envíos deberán proceder de lugares de producción y empacadoras registrados y autorizados por la autoridad fitosanitaria oficial de Egipto, identificados mediante códigos únicos, y deberán cumplir requisitos de trazabilidad que permitan relacionar cada lote con su lugar de producción, empacadora, Certificado Fitosanitario, contenedor y sello o precinto, según corresponda.
     
  • La propuesta contempla además requisitos de muestreo e inspección fitosanitaria, limpieza, lavado y cepillado de los frutos, ausencia de flores, hojas, restos vegetales y suelo, condiciones de embalaje, rotulación, resguardo y transporte, así como inspección fitosanitaria por el Servicio Agrícola y Ganadero al ingreso a Chile.
     
  • Previo al inicio de la primera temporada de exportación, el SAG realizará una verificación técnica en origen destinada a evaluar el cumplimiento de los requisitos establecidos, las condiciones de los lugares de producción y empacadoras, los procedimientos oficiales de certificación fitosanitaria y el programa de vigilancia y monitoreo de Bactrocera zonata y Ceratitis capitata.

 

Para mayor detalle, revisar el documento adjunto a esta notificación.

La medida establece que los envíos deberán estar amparados por un Certificado Fitosanitario Oficial emitido por la Organización Nacional de Protección Fitosanitaria de Egipto, incluyendo declaraciones adicionales para las plagas cuarentenarias asociadas a la vía.
Para el manejo del riesgo de Bactrocera zonata y Ceratitis capitata se establece la aplicación de un tratamiento cuarentenario de frío T107-L, a una temperatura de 1,67 °C o inferior durante 18 días, el cual podrá realizarse en origen o en tránsito. Asimismo, se establecen medidas fitosanitarias específicas para Phytophthora palmivora y requisitos de inspección para las restantes plagascuarentenarias reguladas.Los envíos deberán proceder de lugares de producción y empacadoras registrados y autorizados por la autoridad fitosanitaria oficial de Egipto, identificados mediante códigos únicos, y deberán cumplir requisitos de trazabilidad que permitan relacionar cada lote con su lugar de producción, empacadora, Certificado Fitosanitario, contenedor y sello o precinto, según corresponda.
La propuesta contempla además requisitos de muestreo e inspección fitosanitaria, limpieza, lavado y cepillado de los frutos, ausencia de flores, hojas, restos vegetales y suelo, condiciones de embalaje, rotulación, resguardo y transporte, así como inspección fitosanitaria por el Servicio Agrícola y Ganadero al ingreso a Chile.

title: Proposed amendments to Standards for Recognition of Temporary Standard and Specifications for Foods
description:
The Republic of Korea is proposing to amend the "Standards for Recognition of Temporary Standard and Specifications for Foods".
The regulations on applying for temporary standards and specifications of new food ingredients, food additives, etc. have been improved as following;
1) Revisions regarding fees for applications to approve or modify temporary standards and specifications for food products (under the Enforcement Rule of the Food
Sanitation Act) will be reflected in relevant forms, such as the approval application.
2) The scope of permissible modifications will be expanded, and a new processing timeframe will be established for food ingredients, allowing for changes to the target food products, usage amounts, manufacturing methods, and manufacturers, provided such as changes do not compromise safety.

title: Proposal to modify two of the Lists of Permitted Food Additives (fruit and vegetable cellulose isolate); Proposal to modify the List of Permitted Food Enzymes (nuclease P1); and Proposal to modify the List of Permitted Food Enzymes (3-phytase)
description:
Health Canada's Food and Nutrition Directorate completed premarket assessments of a number of food additive submissions seeking authorization for the use of: 

  • fruit and vegetable cellulose isolate as a stabilizing or thickening agent in cream for whipping at a maximum level of use of 2,000 ppm and as a bodying and texturizing agent or filler in various foods at maximum levels of use that vary according to the food;  
  • nuclease P1 from Penicillium citrinum NP 11-15 be authorized for use as a food enzyme in nucleotide-rich fish hydrolysate and nucleotide-rich yeast extract at a maximum level of “Good Manufacturing Practice” (GMP); and 
  • 3-phytase from Aspergillus niger NPH in plant-based products that resemble dairy products, as well as in plant-based products that resemble dairy-based products at a maximum level of “Good Manufacturing Practice” (GMP). 

 

The results of these premarket assessments support authorizing these additives for their requested uses. Consequently, Health Canada intends to enable the use of these food additives by modifying a number of the List of Permitted Food Additives, as described in this notice. 

The purpose of the information document is to publicly announce the Department's intention in this regard and to provide the appropriate contact information for those wishing to submit an inquiry or new scientific information relevant to the safety of this food additive.

title: Proposal to modify the List of Permitted Food Additives with Other Purposes of Use (chloropentafluoroethane and octafluorocyclobutane)
description:
Health Canada has launched a consultation on a proposal to no longer allow chloropentafluoroethane and octafluorocyclobutane to be used as food additives by removing their respective entries from the List of Permitted Food Additives with Other Purposes of Use, as described in the notice. 

The purpose of the information document is to publicly announce the Department's intention in this regard and to provide the appropriate contact information for those wishing to submit an inquiry or new scientific information relevant to the safety of this food additive.

title: Modification to the List of Permitted Anticaking Agents (silicon dioxide)
description:
Health Canada's Food Directorate completed a premarket assessment of a food additive submission seeking authorization for the use of silicon dioxide as an anticaking agent in nutrient pre-mixes for use in infant formula. 

 

The outcome of the premarket assessment supports authorizing silicon dioxide for use as an anticaking agent in nutrient pre-mixes for use in infant formula at a maximum level of use of Good Manufacturing Practice, with the silicon dioxide residue in the formula as consumed not to exceed 10 ppm. Consequently, Health Canada has extended the use of silicon dioxide as described in the Notice by modifying the List of Permitted Anticaking Agents, effective 29 October 2026. 

 

The purpose of the information document is to publicly announce the Department's decision in this regard and to provide the appropriate contact information for those wishing to submit an inquiry or new scientific information relevant to the safety of this food additive.

title: Partial Amendment Notice (Draft) of Standards and Specifications for Health Functional Foods (Advance Notice No. 2026-512, 23 October 2026)
description:
The proposed amendments seek to:

A. Reorganization of the structural framework of the Standards and Specifications for Health Functional Foods
(Draft Articles I.2, I.3, I.4, I.5, II.1, II.2, II.3, II.4, II.6, and [Annex 4])

  • The provisions for "Collection and Handling of Test Samples" were separated from the general standards and specifications, and "Raw Materials" was relocated to the general manufacturing standards, alongside the removal of unnecessary details and clarification of provisions.

B. Expansion of new ingredients for nutrients and establishment of specifications for ingredients to restructure the management system
(Draft Articles III.1.1, 4), 6), 7), and 8); III.1-1 4); III.1.1-4 4); III.1.1-11 1); III.1.1-16 1), 2), and 3); III.1.1-17 1), 2), and 3); and [Annex 5])

  • Three new ingredients, including calcium L-methylfolate, were added as manufacturing ingredients for folic acid, magnesium, and iron, and component specifications for magnesium and iron ingredients were newly established.

C. Improvement of the microbial specification application method for Ginseng and Red Ginseng concentrates
(Draft Articles III.2.2-1 2) and III.2.2-2 2))

  • The unit for the viable bacterial count specification for concentrates was changed from milliliter (mL) to gram (g).

D. Expansion of manufacturing methods for oils and fats containing EPA and DHA
(Draft Article III.2.2-16 1))

  • Additional manufacturing methods for EPA and DHA-containing oils and fats were permitted to broaden the scope of raw material supply and manufacturing options.

E. Further expansion of the recognized scope of raw materials for mucopolysaccharide protein
(Draft Article III.2.2-32 1) (1))

  • Reflecting scientific evidence secured after re-evaluation, "cartilage tissue of sturgeon and skate" was added to diversify raw materials and broaden manufacturing options, thereby strengthening the competitiveness of related products.

F. Expansion of the daily intake range for probiotics
(Draft Article III.2.2-51 3))

  • The upper limit of the daily intake for probiotics (10 billion CFU) was removed, changing the standard to "100 million CFU or more".

G. Clarification of daily intake for functional ingredients
(Draft Articles III.2.2-33 3), III.2.2-34 3), III.2.2-35 3), III.2.2-36 3), III.2.2-37 3), III.2.2-38 3), III.2.2-39 3), III.2.2-40 3), III.2.2-41 3), III.2.2-42 3), III.2.2-43 3), III.2.2-44 3), III.2.2-45 3), III.2.2-46 3), III.2.2-58 3), III.2.2-59 3), III.2.2-60 3), III.2.2-62 3), III.2.2-63 3), III.2.2-65 3), III.2.2-66 4), and III.2.2-68 3))

  • The daily intake of functional ingredients such as dietary fiber was modified to be based on functional (or marker) components.

title: Partial Amendment Notice (Draft) of Standards and Specifications for Health Functional Foods (Advance Notice No. 2026-513, 23 October 2026)
description:
The proposed amendments seek to:

A. Strengthening common manufacturing standards for functional ingredients (Draft Articles 2.1.3 and 2.2.3)
- Establish specifications for the use of mixed functional ingredients and other ingredients to prevent misuse and side effects and ensure safe intake by reflecting current consumption trends.
B. Revision of intake precautions for three types of functional ingredients (Draft Articles 3.2.2-6 3 & 4, 3.2.2-20 3, 3.2.2-54 3)
- Establish or amend precautions for green tea extract and shark liver oil containing alcoxyglycerol based on the review results of re-evaluations for the safety and functionality of functional ingredients.
- Amend intake precautions for theanine due to instances where it was inappropriately applied, not complying with its functional claim (e.g., “may help relieve tension caused by stress”).

title: Projet de décret modifiant et complétant le décret n° 2-10-473 du 6 septembre 2011 pris pour l'application de certaines dispositions de la loi n° 28-07 relative à la sécurité sanitaire des produits alimentaires
description:
Le présent projet de décret prévoit les amendements suivants :

  • la définition des termes « retrait » et « rappel » des produits ;
  • l’étalonnage et/ou la vérification des dispositifs de mesure ayant une incidence sur la sécurité sanitaire des produits alimentaires ;
  • la fixation d’une liste positive des arômes alimentaires et des auxiliaires technologiques autorisés dans les produits alimentaires ;
  • la suppression de l’obligation d’autorisation des prémélanges, des aliments composés et des aliments complémentaires pour animaux.

Les dispositions concernent également les équipements de mesure ou de surveillance utilisés dans les activités soumises aux exigences sanitaires et les procédures d'agrément des laboratoires privés

proposedEntryIntoForceDateText:
This Communiqué enters into force on the date of its publication with the transitional period until 31 December 2027

Provisional Article

(1) Food businesses operating before the publication date of this Communiqué must comply with the provisions of this Communiqué until 31 December 2027.

(2) Products that comply with the provisions of the Communiqué repealed by Article 17, operated by food businesses operating before the publication date of this Communiqué, may remain on the market for their shelf life, provided that they are placed on the market before 31 December 2027.

title: Implementation Guide on the Updated Regulations on the Importation of Dogs and Cats into the Philippines
description: This Circular is hereby issued to provide the updated  guidelines and implementation procedures for the importation of dogs and cats into the Philippines. It outlines the documentary and animal health requirements, including the approved Sanitary and Phytosanitary Import Clearance (SPSIC), rabies vaccination, parasite treatment, microchip identification, and among others. It must be noted that Philippines now requires Rabies Neutralizing Antibody Titer Test Result for each dog and cat entering the Philippines. Furthermore, Form 1 (Certificate of Animal Vaccination, Antibody Titer and Medication) is a mandatory document required during the application of SPSIC. This Circular also specifies the application process, required documents upon arrival, implementation schedule.

title: Proposal to modify the List of Permitted Supplemental Ingredients (vitamin B6)
description:
Health Canada initiated an evaluation to determine whether revised conditions of use for vitamin B6 in supplemented foods should be proposed based on the publication of an updated scientific opinion on the tolerable upper intake level (UL) for vitamin B6 by the European Food Safety Authority Panel on Nutrition, Novel Foods and Food Allergens (EFSA NDA Panel). Health Canada considered also considered control trials and case reports from the scientific literature, as well as information available in the Canada Vigilance Adverse Reaction Online Database.

The results of this evaluation support the revision of the conditions of use for vitamin B6 including the maximum permitted amounts in supplemented foods as well the threshold levels above which cautionary statements are required on the label.

Therefore, Health Canada proposes modifying the List of Permitted Supplemental Ingredients, as described in the information document cited above.

The purpose of this document is to publicly announce Health Canada’s intention in this regard and to provide the appropriate contact information for those wishing to submit comments, inquiries or new scientific information relevant to the safety of this food additive.

title: Resolución 00021295 del 28 de octubre de 2026, "Por medio de la cual se suspende temporalmente la emisión de documentos zoosanitarios de importación (DZI) para aves vivas, productos y subproductos de riesgo susceptibles de transmitir la enfermedad de Newcastle, procedentes del estado de Santa Catarina, Brasil y se dictan otras disposiciones" (Resolution No. 00021295 of 28 October 2026 temporarily suspending the issuance of animal health import documents (DZI) for live birds, products and by-products at risk of transmitting Newcastle disease, coming from the state of Santa Catarina, Brazil, and issuing other provisions);
description: The notified Resolution temporarily suspends the issuance of animal health import documents (DZI) for live birds, products and by-products at risk of transmitting Newcastle disease, coming from the state of Santa Catarina, Brazil. If live birds or products and by-products of avian origin arrive in the country, the consignment shall be reshipped or destroyed, as appropriate. Entry into the country is also prohibited for such products when covered by animal health import documents (DZI) issued by the Colombian Agricultural Institute (ICA) before the entry into force of the notified Resolution.
